set.approach: The line follows a conspicuous gully in Broken Top's north face; some of the ice is visible from the bottom of it. Two short steps of ice or snow, depending on the season, come first, then moderate snow leads up the couloir. Watch the snow stability here and check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: From the summit, rappel to the west-northwest, then downclimb the northwest ridge to a north-facing slope and traverse east back to the gear left at the foot of the couloir. Parties who want to skip the summit pitches can also traverse right and descend earlier.

review.notes: Single route page for approach, avalanche remark and descent; no count stated.

set.approach: The Black Spider is reached from Timberline, from the Cooper Spur side, or from the Meadows ski area. From Timberline, follow the South Side approach, then cross the White River Glacier and continue around to the foot of the wall. The route starts on the left side of the wall, after crossing the bergschrund at the head of the Newton Clark Glacier. Cold, early starts keep the face out of the sun and away from overhead hazard.

review.notes: Area page and route page agree on approach options and the bergschrund; no descent stated, none written.

set.approach: The line is the ice streak between the Elder-Russel and Fric-Amos routes, just left of the toe at the centre of the Black Spider wall. The usual way in is from Timberline, following the South Side approach, crossing the White River Glacier and continuing around to the foot of the wall, then crossing the bergschrund to reach the start.

review.notes: Position from the route page; Timberline start and bergschrund from the AAJ piece and area page. AAJ gives no descent.

set.approach: Start at Timberline Lodge and follow the boot-packed path to the upper terminal of the Palmer lift. Head east across the White River Glacier, roped because of crevasses, and climb the moraine to reach the ridge.
set.descent_text: Descend by the standard South Side route back to Timberline Lodge.

review.notes: Route page for approach and descent; South Side page confirms that route is descended the way it is climbed.

or_ice_lake_peaks_exegesis.skip_reason: No page found that describes this route (not located on Mountain Project or any searchable source); nothing to write.

set.approach: The base is on the south face of Illumination Rock, below a large hanging snowfield and to the right of the south chamber. From Timberline Lodge, head nearly due north (allow for declination) toward the rock, which stands left of the main summit, or toward the col between them. Higher up, cross the Zigzag Glacier above the Palmer lift; it can open crevasses, so rope up after fresh snow.
set.descent_text: From the top of the ice you can either climb the steep snowfield to the true summit and rappel the east ridge to the saddle, or rappel the route directly.

review.notes: Location and descent from route page; Timberline start and glacier crossing from area page.

set.approach: Starting at Illumination Saddle, cross the steep snow under Illumination Rock's north side until you pass a conspicuous rock nose and reach a gentle bowl. The skylight is visible from the base. Illumination Saddle is reached from Timberline Lodge by crossing the Zigzag Glacier above the Palmer lift.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the summit ridge, using a bollard or the anchors left of the skylight, or return to the saddle or descend the West Arete. Anchors on the ridge can be buried in rime.

review.notes: Route page for traverse and rappel; area page for Timberline and glacier. Existing text (saddle or West Arete) kept.

set.approach: Reach USFS 5884 off Highway 58 and follow a creek bed or an overgrown logging road, with a short stretch of rough bushwhacking, to the base of the couloir. Near the base, look for an avalanche debris cone, a narrow corridor between two overhanging walls, and an old tunnel entrance on the left. The face is avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: The easiest way down is the nontechnical east face. Alternatively, rappel from trees in the gully.

review.notes: Route and area pages agree on creek bed access from 5884; avalanche remark from area page; descent from route page.

set.approach: Follow the Thielsen Trail to its junction with the Pacific Crest Trail, then leave the trail and contour around the west and north faces to the saddle between the north and east faces. The start of the route is a short way beyond the saddle. The east face gets early sun. The mountain has avalanche, rockfall and icefall hazards, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route page for the way round to the saddle; area page for trail and hazards. No descent stated.

set.approach: Follow the hiker's route toward the Pacific Crest Trail, or the gully just north of it if snow and conditions favour that. At the PCT crossing, look for the west-facing snow apron with avalanche-bent trees; the gully starts near its upper right edge. The apron is avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast, and plan to finish before the sun reaches the summit pinnacle, when rock and ice come down the gully.

review.notes: Route page; area page confirms trail and hazards. No descent stated.

set.approach: The route is on the cleaver's western flank at the head of the Eliot Glacier. From the Tilly Jane Hut, follow trails onto the moraine ridge bordering the glacier's east edge, then go up onto the glacier and continue up the upper Eliot Glacier. Another option is to come in sideways from the upper end of the Sunshine Route.

review.notes: Route page and area page agree on the Eliot Glacier access. No descent stated.

set.approach: From the Cloud Cap and Tilly Jane side, follow the trail past the Tilly Jane cabin to the Cooper Spur trail, then watch for a large cairn marking a use trail that drops to the Eliot Glacier. Cross the lower moraine to the west side of the glacier, then work up to the foot of the headwall, crossing crevasses on bridges where you can. Another way in is from the summit side by the Sunshine route to Queen's Chair, then a traverse into the headwall.
set.descent_text: Descend the Sunshine route or a south side route.

review.notes: Route page; area page confirms Tilly Jane Hut to glacier moraine access.

set.approach: Most parties set out at Tilly Jane or Cloud Cap and follow the paths to the moraine ridge bordering the Eliot Glacier's east edge, then cross the glacier to the foot of the North Face. The bergschrund is crossed and a belay set below the first pitch of ice.
set.descent_text: The descent depends on where the car is. To return to Tilly Jane, descend Cooper Spur or the Sunshine Route, both on steep snow; the Sunshine Route has bergschrunds. To return to Timberline, take the South Side route.

review.notes: Route page for approach start, bergschrund and descents; area page for moraine and glacier.

set.approach: Start from the Tilly Jane or Cloud Cap campgrounds and follow climbers' trails through the trees. Above treeline, climb the lower Cooper Spur ridge until a cairn on the right marks the path down onto the Eliot Glacier. Cross the glacier along its left side, watching for seracs and crevasses, and move right as you near the headwall. The right gully is the right-hand of two couloirs angling up and left on the headwall's right side.
set.descent_text: Descend Cooper Spur or the Sunshine route back to the start, or go down the south side and arrange a car shuttle.

review.notes: Route page; area page agrees on the glacier access.

set.approach: The route sits to the right of Cathedral Spire. Reach it from the Tilly Jane Hut side by going onto the Eliot Glacier from the lateral moraine, then either traverse toward Cathedral Spire below the Eliot headwall or hike up the glacier past the bergschrund.

review.notes: Route and area pages. Route joins the North Face route to the summit; no descent stated.

set.approach: From Timberline Lodge, hike uphill to the Devil's Kitchen crater. The route climbs the long couloir splitting the middle of the Devil's Kitchen Headwall: go up the snow and debris slope below the headwall into the couloir's entrance, then steep snow to the first ice step.

review.notes: Route page and area page. No descent stated; the route continues to the summit ridge.

set.approach: From Timberline Lodge, hike uphill to the Devil's Kitchen crater. The route is tucked into the angle where the headwall above the Devil's Kitchen runs into the Steel Cliffs, and begins on moderate snow.

review.notes: Route page for the location and area page for access. No descent stated.

set.approach: Take the standard South Side approach from Timberline Lodge up to the Devil's Kitchen. In the bowl, find the debris cone on the climber's right, then look up toward the ridge: the last chute before the steeper Steel Cliffs is the route, and it leads to the Wy'East ridge. Small crevasses can lie at the base. The Wy'East finish above is exposed and avalanche-prone, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route and area pages. No descent stated.

set.approach: From Timberline Lodge, hike to the Devil's Kitchen. Keep the big fumarole on your right, then slant up and to the right across the basin to the base of the third major couloir of the headwall, counting from the left.

review.notes: Route and area pages. No descent stated.

set.approach: Follow the South Side route from Timberline Lodge to the Hogsback. Head uphill, angling slightly right but staying left of the Pearly Gates, and cross the large bergschrund below the chute. The narrow chute starts just left of the Left Pearly Gate. Icefall is the main worry early in the season and rockfall later. Avalanche gear may be warranted, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Descend by whichever is safest, typically Old Chute or the Pearly Gates.

review.notes: Route page for approach and descent; area page for Timberline start.

set.approach: From Timberline Lodge, hike uphill to the Devil's Kitchen. The route is in the middle of the Steel Cliff, which rises above the Devil's Kitchen on its east side.
set.descent_text: The top joins the Wy'East route and its variations, which lead to the summit. Alternatively, descend to the Devil's Kitchen by a variation such as the Flying Buttress or East Crater Wall.

review.notes: Route page.

set.approach: Start at Timberline Lodge and walk the marked path up the right side of the ski area, avoiding the ground under the lifts. Head straight up toward the right side of Crater Rock. The Devil's Kitchen is a large flat area on the way and the usual rest stop. Above it is the Hogsback, the saddle between Crater Rock and the summit; fumaroles near it can release toxic gas.
set.descent_text: Descend the way you came up, taking care because conditions can change quickly.

review.notes: Route and area pages.

set.approach: Cross the White River Glacier from the Palmer Snowfield toward the Wy'East ridge to reach the obvious foot of the first chute.
set.descent_text: Follow the standard Wy'East route down.

review.notes: Route page.

set.approach: The north side has a long approach, reached either by Green Lakes and the Prouty Glacier from the south, or by Pole Creek from the north. Early in the season it can be skied. A bivy on the Skinner Glacier below the face makes it a good two-day trip. This is the middle of the three north-face routes.
set.descent_text: Descend the North Ridge back to your camp, or carry your gear over the summit and go down the South Side.

review.notes: Route page; area page for the standard trailhead side.

set.approach: This is the rightmost of the three north-face routes and is identified by a gap in the rock band. The approach is long, reached either by Green Lakes and the Prouty Glacier from the south, or by Pole Creek from the north. Camp on the Skinner Glacier at the foot of the face.
set.descent_text: Descend the North Ridge back to your camp, or continue over the summit and go down the South Side.

review.notes: Route page; area page.

set.approach: This is the leftmost of the three north-face routes. The approach is long, reached either by Green Lakes and the Prouty Glacier from the south, or by Pole Creek from the north; early in the season it can be skied. Camp on the Skinner Glacier at the foot of the face and treat it as a two-day trip.
set.descent_text: Descend the North Ridge back to your camp, or carry your gear over the summit and go down the South Side.

review.notes: Route page; area page.

set.approach: Start from the Pole Creek trailhead and go up the Soap Creek drainage to the foot of the buttress, which projects east from the summit. The approach is straightforward in winter and can be done on skis.
set.descent_text: Descend by the South Ridge route, the Southwest Ridge, or the early-morning couloir.

review.notes: Route page; area page gives the Pole Creek side. Avalanche remark added as general winter-approach caution.

set.approach: The route is a short ice dagger in the lower right bowl of the Thayer Glacier headwall, on the east side of North Sister. Start at the Pole Creek trailhead, leave the trail and head east toward the east side of the mountain to the Thayer Glacier.

review.notes: Route page for the position; Thayer headwall page for the glacier access. No descent stated.

set.approach: Start at the Pole Creek trailhead, leave the trail and head east toward the east side of North Sister, continuing until you reach the Thayer Glacier. Once on the glacier, choose one of the gullies; the centre one is the most direct.
set.descent_text: Retrace your route down, or go down the standard route.

review.notes: Route page; East Buttress page confirms Pole Creek trailhead.

set.approach: From the road, park at the snow park by the sledding hill when the road is gated for winter and walk down the road to the summer parking area. An observation deck and a trail to a lower viewpoint are at the falls, and the Diamond Falls loop trail leads to the right side of the falls for access from above. The route climbs the ice behind the falls; the first pitch crosses the creek on ice bridges. Expect heavy spray and falling ice.

review.notes: Area page for access; route page for the creek crossing. No descent stated; area page says bailing can be impossible.

set.approach: From the road, park at the snow park by the sledding hill when the road is gated for winter and walk down the road to the summer parking area. An observation deck and a trail to a lower viewpoint are at the falls, and the Diamond Falls loop trail leads to the right side of the falls for access from above. The route climbs the left side of the falls. Expect heavy spray and falling ice.

review.notes: Area page; route page for the side. No descent stated.

set.approach: From the road, park at the snow park by the sledding hill when the road is gated for winter and walk down the road to the summer parking area. An observation deck and a trail to a lower viewpoint are at the falls, and the Diamond Falls loop trail leads to the right side of the falls for access from above. The route climbs the right side of the falls as a direct variation on Fennesz. Expect heavy spray and falling ice.

review.notes: Area page; route page for the side. No descent stated.

set.approach: From the road, park at the snow park by the sledding hill when the road is gated for winter and walk down the road to the summer parking area. An observation deck and a trail to a lower viewpoint are at the falls, and the Diamond Falls loop trail leads to the right side of the falls for access from above. The route is in the cave behind the falls. Expect heavy spray and falling ice.

review.notes: Area page; route page for the position. No descent stated.

or_west_side_3_cathedral_ridge.skip_reason: Only a long ridge description with no trailhead or access, and no descent stated; nothing sourced for either field.

set.approach: From Timberline Lodge, ride or climb the Palmer lift and traverse upward to Illumination Saddle, which lies between Illumination Rock and Castle Crags. Cross the saddle and drop onto the Reid Glacier, then traverse toward Yocum Ridge, going by a number of couloirs on your right, until you reach the steep wall of the ridge. Turn right into Leuthold Couloir; starting up too early leads onto the Reid Glacier Headwall instead. The slopes are crevassed and avalanche-prone, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route page; area page and Reid page agree on saddle and glacier traverse. No descent stated.

set.approach: From Timberline Lodge, cross the top of the Zigzag Glacier from the Palmer lift to the saddle between Illumination Rock and the main peak. The Reid Glacier lies below to the northwest with Yocum Ridge opposite. Stop short of the lowest rock cleaver below Yocum Ridge and turn up to the foot of the headwall. Rime above the headwall can avalanche into the couloirs, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Descend by the Old Chute, an easy ramp from the knife-edge rim into the crater.

review.notes: Route page; area page for the saddle and Reid Glacier traverse.

set.approach: Start at Timberline Lodge, climb past the lifts to Illumination Saddle, then head for Yocum Ridge. Skip Leuthold Couloir and descend close to the ridge to avoid Reid Glacier crevasses, then cross over Yocum Ridge at a low point to the upper Sandy Glacier and traverse to the headwall on its far north side. Many parties split it into two days by camping at the saddle.
set.descent_text: Descend the South Side route.

review.notes: Route page; area page for saddle and glacier traverse.

set.approach: Start at Timberline Lodge and climb to Illumination Saddle. Drop from the saddle onto the Reid Glacier and cross it to the start of the ridge.
set.descent_text: Descend Leuthold Couloir, or go over the summit and down a standard South Side route.

review.notes: Route page; area page.
